items.headline: Markets Closed for Weekend; Friday Saw Mixed Close Amid Rate Hike Aftermath
items.summary: U.S. equity markets are closed today, Sunday, September 20, 2026. The last trading session on Friday, September 18, 2026, ended mixed as Wall Street continued to digest the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike, rising bond yields, and volatile oil prices. Technology and healthcare sectors showed strength, while utilities and financial services lagged.

items.headline: Strategy Inc. (formerly MicroStrategy)
items.summary: Led gainers as Bitcoin reclaimed $80,000 and the SEC cleared a path for tokenized stock trading.

items.headline: Sandisk
items.summary: A big winner, driven by its upcoming inclusion in the S&P 100 and continued strength in memory pricing.

items.headline: Netflix
items.summary: Slipped after Wells Fargo downgraded the stock, citing worrying viewership trends and a lack of breakout hits.

items.headline: Federal Reserve's Rate Hike Continues to Ripple Through Markets
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's quarter-point rate hike earlier in the week, its first in three years, continued to influence market sentiment, with expectations of one or two additional hikes before year-end.

items.headline: 10-Year Treasury Yield Climbs to 5.00%
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.00%, a level not seen since 2023, increasing borrowing costs and making bonds relatively more attractive. The 2-year Treasury yield also climbed to 4.76%.

items.headline: Tech and Healthcare Lead, Utilities and Financials Lag
items.summary: Healthcare (+1.56%) and Technology (+1.03%) were the best-performing sectors. Conversely, Utilities (-2.95%) and Financial Services (-2.29%) were among the worst performers.

items.headline: Warren Buffett Steps Down as Berkshire Hathaway Chairman
items.summary: Investing legend Warren Buffett announced his decision to step down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after 56 years, with his son Howard Buffett set to take over the role. Greg Abel remains CEO.

items.headline: Mixed Economic Data Released
items.summary: U.S. industrial production was flat in August, missing expectations, while initial jobless claims fell to a six-week low of 196,000. August retail sales showed a 1.2% increase from the previous month.
